title: Expose the limit of the first approach
before: The learner understands a simple way to do the task.
after: They can explain why a change is needed.
sequence: Try the simple approach on one concrete case.
Show where it stops meeting the goal.
Change the part responsible for that limitation.

source.title: The paradox of the derivative
source.locator: Position and Velocity → Rates of Change

observation: The lesson contrasts speed at an instant with measurements across two times, then examines shorter intervals.
interpretation: A limitation gives the next idea a reason to exist; that structure can transfer beyond calculus.
example: A single car snapshot cannot reveal its speed. Comparing two times provides the missing information.
avoid: Changing the task while comparing solutions.
check: Can the learner identify which part of the first approach causes the limitation?
